info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package benchmark is one honest score for any model, on the tests everyone quotes.

post.summary: Stores the per-item rows of a published run, so the board's measured column, history and compare read the items behind a number the platform already publishes.
post.description:
Stores the per-item rows of a published run, so the board's
measured column, history and compare read the items behind a number the
platform already publishes.

Only a SuperAdmin acting in org admin may import; anyone else is refused 403,
and the refusal is audited.

The rows are FOR A CLAIM: the platform must publish a claim for the model on
the benchmark whose source names the run (a research run URL whose id is run),
and the rows must score that claim to within 0.05 points, or the import is
refused 422 saying which. A run is imported once (409 after), every item id is
unique and carries an answer, and a lower-is-better benchmark is refused 422:
its score is a rate the board does not read as accuracy.

The trail takes the import's intent, naming the run and its counts, before the
first row lands.

get.summary: Is the canonical benchmarks this arena reads — the id, title, axis, item count, upstream source and direction of each, with native marking the ones the standardized harness runs today.
get.description:
Is the canonical benchmarks this arena reads — the id, title, axis, item
count, upstream source and direction of each, with native marking the ones the
standardized harness runs today. The first 14 are the public set every major
provider reports; the next 4 are the tests coding agents are judged on —
DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SWE-Atlas QnA and SWE-Bench Pro v2 — published as
claims; the rest are the Decision Suite, scored by Kai's own harness and
published as claims citing the research run each number came from.

direction is "higher" or "lower": which way a score improves, and so which way
the leaderboard orders its rows. Every score is a percentage; a latency is a
fact about serving and lives in the research plane's runs, not here.

These ids are the vocabulary the rest of the surface takes: a run and a claim
name them, and the leaderboard and compare read them from ?benchmark=. The
catalog is deployment-wide and identical for every caller — there is no tenant
in it.

get.summary: Lists the effective claims the caller may read, each labelled with the org that made it and the user who recorded it.
get.description:
Lists the effective claims the caller may read, each labelled with the
org that made it and the user who recorded it.

Anyone reads the public claims. A signed-in caller also reads its own org's
private ones. No caller reads another org's private claims — a SuperAdmin
acting in that org included, since acting in an org is not membership of it.
Rows under org "admin" are the platform's own curated readings: the compiled
seed and any correction a SuperAdmin wrote.

Effective values only. The history of a key lives in the append-only file and
is not what this op is for; a list that returned every superseded row would
make the common question the hard one.

parameters.name: Benchmark
parameters.description: Benchmark filters to one benchmark id. Empty returns every benchmark.

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Model filters to one model. Empty returns every model.

parameters.name: Provider
parameters.description:
Provider filters to one lab or leaderboard — the way to read what a single
source claims across every model it covers.

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description:
Source filters to one citation, which is the finest grain there is: a
source is what makes two claims about one model independent rather than a
restatement of each other.

parameters.name: Protocol
parameters.description:
Protocol filters by HOW a claim was scored, so provider cards can be read
apart from third parties running their own harness.

parameters.name: Org
parameters.description:
Org filters to the claims one org made; "admin" reads the platform's own.
It narrows what the caller may already read and never widens it.

post.summary: Records claims for the caller's org: one to correct a number, many to import a leaderboard.
post.description:
Records claims for the caller's org: one to correct a number, many to
import a leaderboard. Any signed-in caller may write; a caller with no verified
principal is refused 401.

The org and the author are the verified caller's. Nothing in the body names
either, and a body that tries is not read. Claims are private to that org unless
visibility is "public". Writing as org "admin" curates the leaderboard, so it
takes a SuperAdmin; anyone else acting there is refused 403, and the refusal is
audited.

Every row must carry a Source, because a claim without its citation is a
number nobody can check, and a benchmark id from /catalog, because an unknown
id would sit in the store invisible to every read. A row names its benchmark,
model, provider and protocol in at most 128 characters each, cites a source of
at most 2048 bytes, and scores a percentage from 0 to 100; a row outside that is
rejected by number.

A request carries at most 500 rows in at most 1 MiB (413 past either), and an
org writes at most 2000 rows per UTC day (429 past that, and nothing from the
request is written).

The trail takes the call's intent, naming every row, BEFORE the first row
lands; a trail that cannot take it answers 503 and nothing is written. A second
record then names which rows were stored and which failed.

Writes are append-only, so this never destroys the value it replaces. A
vendor restating a score leaves both rows on disk, which is how the restating
itself becomes visible.

post.summary: Publishes an org's public claims onto the leaderboard: each one that matches is copied, as it stands, into the platform's own claims, with the org it came from kept in from.
post.description:
Publishes an org's public claims onto the leaderboard: each one that
matches is copied, as it stands, into the platform's own claims, with the org it
came from kept in from.

Publication is a SuperAdmin act. The board is the platform's reading, so an
org's claim — public or not — never reaches it on its own; this is how one
does, on purpose and on the record. Only a SuperAdmin acting in org admin may
call it. Anyone else is refused 403, a SuperAdmin acting in another org
included, and the refusal is audited.

It reads only the org's PUBLIC claims, the same rows anyone reads at
/v1/benchmark/claims?org=; a private claim is not the platform's to publish. The
copy keeps the benchmark, provider, model, score, protocol and source, so the
published number is the filed number and the citation still names the run it
came from. A claim already published exactly as it stands is counted unchanged
and written again never, so promoting twice is free; one the org has restated
since is published at its new value.

The org's daily write bound applies to the platform's rows, and the trail
takes the call's intent, naming every row, before the first lands.

get.summary: Is the ONLY valid arm-vs-arm test: it pairs the two models on the items BOTH completed, and answers rescue and damage counts with an exact-McNemar p.
get.description:
Is the ONLY valid arm-vs-arm test: it pairs the two models on the items
BOTH completed, and answers rescue and damage counts with an exact-McNemar p.

Pairing is what prevents the subset artifact — comparing one model's easy subset
against another's full run — so n_common, not either arm's own coverage, is the
number to read this by.

Both a and b are required. The benchmark defaults to gpqa_diamond.

parameters.name: benchmark
parameters.description: Benchmark is the catalog id to compare on, defaulting to gpqa_diamond.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: A is the first model id. It is required.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: B is the second model id. It is required.

get.summary: Returns each model's measured score per run over time, oldest first, with the change between runs.
get.description:
Returns each model's measured score per run over time, oldest first,
with the change between runs.

This is the counterweight to a leaderboard: the board shows the latest run
because that is what "how good is it" means, and a single latest number cannot
distinguish a model that has always been strong from one that just improved,
or from one that regressed after a provider changed something. Both matter for
routing, and only one of them is visible on a board.

Runs with no id — attempts recorded before runs existed — group under the
empty run, which is honestly what they are: one undated measurement.

parameters.name: Benchmark
parameters.description: Benchmark is the catalog id to read, defaulting to gpqa_diamond.

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Model filters to one model. Empty returns every model measured.

get.summary: Answers one row per model for the benchmark named — what our own harness measured, beside what the vendor claims, and the gap between them.
get.description:
Answers one row per model for the benchmark named — what our own
harness measured, beside what the vendor claims, and the gap between them.

The gap is the point of the arena; provider-reported claims have run materially
hot against one standardized harness.

The two planes are NEVER blended, and that is the rule to read the rows by: a
model we have measured but no vendor has claimed for shows published null, a
model with only a claim shows measured null, and gap exists only where both do.

Published, Claims, Spread and Mean read the platform's own public claims (org
"admin") and nothing else, whoever asks. Other orgs' claims are at
/v1/benchmark/claims, labelled, and reach this board only when a SuperAdmin
publishes them: writing under org admin, or promoting an org's public claims
with POST /v1/benchmark/claims/promote, which keeps the org they came from in
the row's from.

Rows are best first. A benchmark whose score improves downward — a false-alarm
rate, a share of answers that moved — is ordered lowest first, and the answer
says which with direction.

n is coverage and is not decoration: two measured numbers taken over different
item counts are not comparable, so read the row's n before reading its accuracy.

parameters.name: benchmark
parameters.description: Benchmark is the catalog id to read, defaulting to gpqa_diamond.

get.summary: Are the router blends available to compose from — a named set of model arms, the rank they escalate through and the panel width that bounds fan-out — each named for the model layer as enso-<name>.
get.description:
Are the router blends available to compose from — a named set of model
arms, the rank they escalate through and the panel width that bounds fan-out —
each named for the model layer as enso-<name>.

The first row is the reference blend: a worked example written in models we
name, published as an example of the FORM. It is deliberately not the
composition of a Hanzo-served tier — the tier name exists to abstract that — so
fork it and swap arms by what the leaderboard measures on your own tasks rather
than reading it as a disclosure.

The rows after it are the caller's org's stored blends, by name, the latest
version of each. Anyone reads the reference; only a member of the org reads the
org's own, and a SuperAdmin acting in an org it does not belong to reads what a
stranger reads.

post.summary: Stores a router blend for the caller's org — its name, its arms, the rank they escalate through and the panel fan-out width — and answers with the stored blend and the enso-<name> it would be resolved under.
post.description:
Stores a router blend for the caller's org — its name, its arms, the
rank they escalate through and the panel fan-out width — and answers with the
stored blend and the enso-<name> it would be resolved under.

Storing is not serving: the model layer resolves no stored preset, and the
answer's note says so.

Any signed-in caller may compose; a caller with no verified principal is refused
401. Owner, At and By are the server's, whatever the body says, so a blend is
never stored as another org's. Posting a name the org already holds replaces
that blend; an org holds at most 100 names and stores at most 500 versions per
UTC day (429 past that).

Defaults fill the shape rather than refusing it: an omitted rank becomes the arms
in declared order and a panel below 1 becomes 1. A blend with no name or no arms
is a 400. A name is the part after enso-: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and
inner hyphens, never one of Hanzo's own tiers (auto, flash, pro, ultra, free,
embed) and never beginning with enso-, or it is a 422. So is a blend of more
than 32 arms, an arm named twice or past 128 characters, a rank naming an arm
the blend does not declare, a panel wider than the rank, or a note past 1024
characters.

post.summary: Answers what the arena already holds for a model on each benchmark asked about, and spends nothing.
post.description:
Answers what the arena already holds for a model on each benchmark asked
about, and spends nothing.

For a benchmark the store holds attempts for, the answer is the model's latest
run — its id, when it was recorded, its accuracy and how many items it covered
— served from the attempts already recorded. A measurement held is never run
again from here.

For a benchmark it holds none for, nothing is queued, because this arena has
no executor: the answer says so and names the harness that measures the
benchmark, or, where none here does, the import a published run's items take.
There is no flag to force a run, because nothing here would act on it.

Any signed-in caller may ask; a caller with no verified principal is refused
401. The answer names the caller's verified org and user — nothing in the
body names either — and stores nothing.

Validation is up front and total — a request with no model is a 400, one with
no benchmarks is a 400, and any benchmark id outside the catalog is a 422
naming exactly which ids were unknown.

direction.description:
Direction is "higher" when a higher score is better and "lower" when a
lower one is: a false-alarm rate, a share of answers that moved. The
leaderboard orders its rows by it.

id.description: the id every other op on this surface takes

items.description: how many items it holds, when the set is fixed

native.description: whether the standardized harness runs it today

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the canonical test id the claim is about, from /catalog.

evidence.description: Evidence are the evidence uris the claim rests on, at most 64.

model.description: Model is the system the score is claimed for.

protocol.description:
Protocol records HOW it was scored — provider-reported, agentic,
third-party-leaderboard — so a provider card is never read as a measurement.

provider.description:
Provider is who the claim belongs to — the lab or leaderboard whose number
this is.

runs.description: Runs are the research run ids the claim rests on, at most 64.

score.description: Score is the reported aggregate, as a percentage.

source.description: Source is the citation the row was read from. Required.

at.description: At is when a stored row was recorded. Zero for a seed row.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the canonical test id the claim is about, from /catalog.

by.description: By is the verified user who recorded a stored row. Empty for a seed row.

evidence.description:
Evidence are the evidence uris the claim rests on
(GET /v1/research/evidence?uri=).

from.description:
From is the org a curator row was promoted from: the org that filed the
claim before a SuperAdmin published it. Empty on every other row.

model.description: Model is the system the score is claimed for.

org.description:
Org is the org that made the claim. "admin" is the platform's own curated
reading; any other org is that org's claim, not the platform's. Empty on an
unattributed row.

origin.description:
Origin is "seed" for a compiled row, "stored" for one a verified caller
wrote through this surface, and "unattributed" for a stored row no verified
caller vouches for, which never reaches the leaderboard.

protocol.description:
Protocol records HOW it was scored — provider-reported, agentic,
third-party-leaderboard — so a provider card is never read as a measurement.

provider.description:
Provider is who the claim belongs to — the lab or leaderboard whose number
this is.

runs.description:
Runs are the research run ids the claim rests on
(GET /v1/research/runs?id=).

score.description: Score is the reported aggregate, as a percentage.

source.description: Source is the citation the row was read from.

visibility.description:
Visibility is "public", readable by anyone, or "private", readable by Org's
own members only. Only the curator's public claims reach the leaderboard.

answer.description:
Answer is what the model answered, as the harness extracted it. Required:
an item with no answer was not attempted.

correct.description: Correct is the harness's verdict on Answer.

item.description: Item is the benchmark's own id for the question or case.

ciHigh.description:
CIHigh is the upper bound of that interval. Wilson rather than the normal
approximation because the normal one produces bounds past 100 exactly where
benchmark scores live — at 194/198 that is the top of the board, not a
corner case.

ciLow.description:
CILow and CIHigh are the 95% Wilson interval on Measured, in percent. They
are what makes the score comparable: at n=198 a 98% carries roughly ±2
points, so most differences at the top of a board are not distinguishable
and a bare number implies a precision it does not have. Absent when there
is no measurement.

claims.description:
Claims is how many independent claims the platform holds for this model on
this benchmark. More than one means several sources reported it.

evidence.description:
Evidence are the evidence uris the Published claim rests on
(GET /v1/research/evidence?uri=).

from.description:
From is the org whose claim Published was promoted from, when a SuperAdmin
published another org's claim rather than writing one under org admin:
"hanzo" on a row Hanzo measured and the platform published.

mean.description:
Mean is the unweighted average of every claim, which answers a different
question from Published: what the field says on average, rather than what
the vendor says about itself. With one claim the two are equal.

measuredAt.description: MeasuredAt is when the run behind Measured was recorded.

n.description: coverage — NEVER compare across different n

protocol.description: how the vendor scored their claim: single-attempt, pass@k or agentic

published.description: the platform's selected claim % (nil if none)

run.description:
Run names the measurement Measured came from, and MeasuredAt is when it
ran. A score with no date is not a fact about a model, it is a fact about
a model on a day — and models change, so the date is what makes the number
checkable rather than merely quoted.

runs.description:
Runs are the research run ids the Published claim rests on
(GET /v1/research/runs?id=).

spread.description:
Spread is the distance between the highest and lowest of them, nil when
there is only one. It is the disagreement AMONG sources, which a single
Published number cannot show — signal in the same way the
published-minus-measured gap is.

model.description: Model is the system these runs measured.

points.description: Points is every run, oldest first.

trend.description:
Trend is the change from the first run to the last, absent when there has
only been one. It answers the question a list of points makes you compute.

arms.description: the blend — model ids from the arena

at.description:
At is when this version was stored. Set by the server; a value sent is not
read. Zero on the reference blend.

by.description:
By is the verified user who stored it. Set by the server; a value sent is
not read.

name.description: the part after enso-: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, at most 64

owner.description: the org the blend belongs to: the writer's verified org, never a value sent

at.description: At is when the run was recorded.

delta.description:
Delta is the change in score from the previous run for this model, absent
on the first. It is the number the whole surface exists to make visible.

n.description:
N is how many items the run covered. Two runs are only comparable at the
same n, which is why it travels with every point rather than being assumed.

run.description: Run is the measurement id these attempts were recorded under.

score.description: Score is accuracy over the items this run covered, as a percentage.

data.description: Data is one row per benchmark, in the catalog's own order.

total.description: Total is how many rows Data holds.

data.description:
Data is one row per (org, benchmark, model, SOURCE) — every independent
claim, not one per model. Effective values only: the row that wins after
layering for each key, never the superseded readings behind it.

total.description: Total is how many rows Data holds.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the catalog id these histories are about.

data.description: Data is one entry per model, ordered by model name.

total.description: Total is how many models Data holds.

at.description:
At is when the run was measured, RFC3339. Empty is now. It orders the
model's runs in history and picks the latest for the board, so a backfill
names the date it measured.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the catalog id the run measured. Required.

data.description: Data is every item the run scored, at most 20000.

model.description:
Model is the model the run measured, as the published claim names it.
Required.

run.description:
Run is the research run the rows came from: the id the claim's source
names. Required.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the catalog id they were stored under.

claim.description: Claim is the published score the rows itemize.

imported.description: Imported is how many items were stored.

model.description: Model is the model they measured.

run.description: Run is the research run they came from.

score.description: Score is the rows' accuracy, in percent: what Measured now reads.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the catalog id these rows are about.

direction.description:
Direction is "higher" or "lower": which way this benchmark's score
improves, and so which way Rows is ordered.

rows.description:
Rows is one per model, best first in Direction: measured rows by their
measurement, then claim-only rows by their published score, ties by model.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the catalog id this answer is about.

harness.description:
Harness is the harness that measures this benchmark for the arena, by
repository. Empty when none does, and then a measurement arrives only as a
published run's items imported through POST /v1/benchmark/attempts.

latest.description:
Latest is the model's latest run on this benchmark — its run id, when it
was recorded, its accuracy and how many items it covered — read from the
attempts the store already holds. Null when the store holds none.

note.description:
Note says in a sentence what the answer means: a held measurement served
rather than spent again, or nothing queued and why.

by.description: By is the verified user who asked.

data.description: Data is one answer per benchmark, in the order the request named them.

model.description: Model is the model asked about.

org.description: Org is the caller's verified org.

a.description: A is the first model id.

a_correct.description: ACorrect is how many of those common items A got right.

b.description: B is the second model id.

b_correct.description: BCorrect is how many of those common items B got right.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the catalog id the two arms were compared on.

mcnemar_p.description:
McnemarP is the two-sided exact binomial p on the discordant pairs. It is 1
when nothing is discordant, which is "no evidence of a difference", not an
error.

n_common.description:
NCommon is how many items BOTH arms completed. It is the denominator, and
the reason this comparison is valid where a raw accuracy difference is not.

net_a_minus_b.description: NetAMinusB is the two rescue counts subtracted — A's advantage in items.

rescue_a_over_b.description: RescueAOverB is how many items A got right and B got wrong.

rescue_b_over_a.description: RescueBOverA is how many items B got right and A got wrong.

data.description: Data is the reference blend, then the caller's org's stored blends by name.

note.description: Note says what storing does and does not promise.

preset.description:
Preset is the blend as stored: defaults filled in, Owner the caller's
verified org, At and By the server's.

served_as.description:
ServedAs is enso-<name>: the model id a router would resolve this blend
under.

benchmark.description: Benchmark narrows the promotion to one catalog id. Empty takes every one.

model.description: Model narrows it to one model. Empty takes every one.

org.description:
Org is the org whose public claims to publish. It is required, and it is
never "admin": the platform's own claims are on the board already.

protocol.description:
Protocol narrows it to one way of scoring — hanzo-measured,
oracle-ceiling. Empty takes every one.

source.description: Source narrows it to one citation. Empty takes every one.

data.description:
Data is the platform rows this call wrote, in benchmark, model and source
order.

from.description: From is the org the claims were promoted from.

promoted.description: Promoted is how many claims this call published.

rejected.description: Rejected names the claims that were not stored, and why.

unchanged.description:
Unchanged is how many matched and were published already, exactly as
they stand, so nothing was written for them.

data.description:
Data is the claims to record. One row is a correction; many is an import.
There is no separate bulk endpoint because there is no separate operation:
importing a leaderboard and fixing one number are the same write.

visibility.description:
Visibility is who may read every row in Data: "private", the default, keeps
them to the caller's org; "public" shows them to anyone. Restating a claim
with the other value moves it.

org.description: Org is the org the rows were recorded under: the caller's own.

recorded.description: Recorded is how many rows were written.

rejected.description: Rejected names the rows that were not, and why.

visibility.description: Visibility is who may read them.

benchmarks.description:
Benchmarks are the catalog ids to ask about. At least one is required, and
every id must be in the catalog.

model.description:
Model is the model to ask about, by the id its attempts are stored under.
Required.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
